source.title: Probing for Representation Manifolds in Superposition

page_placements.theme: Geometric measures, task values and causal interpretation

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and applies a method for finding multidimensional representation manifolds in an LLM, refining the one-dimensional-direction account. It does not test toy-model superposition directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports manifold probing and a steering intervention. Numerical test R2 values and steering probabilities are not stated in the text provided, so figure-only values are not inferred. Results attributed to cited prior work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a methods paper (the Manifold Probe). Its Llama 2-7b results still bear on V6. Time and space concepts are linearly represented by several features, not one direction: Figure 3 shows many features with positive test R2, and the space concept has three highly predictable features. This suggests continuous concepts occupy multidimensional subspaces. It does not show those subspaces are irreducible, and the probe assumes the additive superposition model it applies.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The author presents the Manifold Probe as a supervised tool for finding representation manifolds in superposition. On time and space in Llama 2-7b it finds many linearly represented features beyond the concept values. Varimax-rotated features separate decades and U.S. states. Steering along the time manifold influences year completions, which the author takes as evidence the manifold is causally used. The author treats multidimensional manifolds as compatible with superposition, not as refuting it.
record.recipe_differences: This is a supervised manifold-probing method applied to continuous concepts in an LLM, not a reproduction of the original toy-network method or its sparsity and geometry sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering efficacy and optimal intervention layer depend on the work's release decade and the target year; efficacy falls to baseline at layer 20 and beyond.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding steering vectors traced along the learned time manifold raises the probability of year completions near the target. Efficacy peaks around layers 8-14 and falls to baseline at layer 20 and beyond.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Probe-derived representation manifolds for continuous concepts in LLMs are causally used by the model, in a layer-dependent way.

record.problems: The reported evidence is from one model. Numerical test R2 values and steering efficacy values are not available in the supplied text, and steering efficacy varies substantially by layer and target.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows were made for test R2 values or for probabilities shown only in figures because the supplied text does not state their numerical values.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, phase transition or geometry analysis.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity competition.
No alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
No measure of spread across neurons and no SAE recovery. Superposition is assumed, not tested.
Only two continuous concepts (time, space) in one model. No irreducibility test separating a multidimensional feature from several 1-D features. No binary or discrete features.

missing.what: Number of linearly represented features per concept per layer: ranked test R2 values above zero. Predictability rises through the first half of the layers and then levels off. Space has three features considerably more predictable than the rest.
Test R2 of the first five time features and first three space features at layer 16 (figure-only values).
The top time feature is close to the identity (year) feature and tracks the direct ridge-regression R2.

record.verdict_notes: Single model, single author, preprint. All numerical results are figure-only. The record's 'challenges' label for V6 is too strong: the paper does not test whether the subspaces are irreducible, and its Varimax decade/state features are consistent with many 1-D directions. The text has an apparent slip: 'In the time representations, the highest ranked feature… higher… than latitude and longitude' should presumably read 'space'. The probe dimension is chosen by the author, not inferred from the data.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature sparsity sweep, or regular-geometry transition are tested.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or feature-capacity competition is tested.
No alternative causes of polysemantic neurons are tested.
The study does not measure feature spread across neurons or test SAE recovery.
No SAE features or claims about their completeness, stability, or canonical status are tested.

The paper finds multidimensional manifolds for continuous concepts in one LLM, but does not establish that all superposed features in LLMs are multidimensional or compare one-dimensional with multidimensional representations across models.

rows.subject: Llama 2-7b
rows.operation_detail: Fit a three-dimensional Manifold Probe to time representations and use the learned manifold for steering.

conditions.value: release time of songs, movies and books

rows.measure: Dimension of the learned time manifold
rows.note: The paper says it fit three-dimensional manifolds at each layer for the steering experiment.
rows.check: The three-dimensional manifold is the author's chosen probe dimension (d=3) for the steering experiment, not a measured finding. It is a setting, not a result row.

rows.subject: Llama 2-7b
rows.operation_detail: Apply Varimax rotation to the learned features.

conditions.value: release time of songs, movies and books

rows.measure: Geometry and interpretability of rotated features
rows.value: The rotated features approximately separate decades from the 1950s to the 2010s.
rows.note: The rotation is described as aiming to make features approximately sparse.
rows.check: Varimax rotation is an interpretability choice that makes features approximately sparse. The rotated decade features are approximately linearly separated directions, so this does not show whether the time representation is irreducibly multidimensional or several 1-D features.

rows.subject: Llama 2-7b
rows.operation_detail: Apply Varimax rotation to the learned features.

conditions.value: geographic coordinates of places in the U.S.A.

rows.measure: Geometry and interpretability of rotated features
rows.value: Many rotated features localize on particular U.S. states, which the paper describes as approximately linearly separated.
rows.note: The rotated features are described as approximately sparse.
rows.check: Same issue as R2. State-localized rotated features show several directions tied to the space concept, but are compatible with many separate 1-D features. The row does not test dimensionality.

rows.subject: Llama 2-7b
rows.operation_detail: Add the learned time-manifold steering vector at the last-token residual stream activation, with alpha = 100.

conditions.value: 1,400 test-set works, with 200 from each decade
probability of completing within two years of the target

rows.value: figure only; text says efficacy peaks at layers 8 and 14 depending on the work's release decade, drops sharply after layer 15, and reaches baseline at layer 20 and beyond
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations are shown in Figure 7; numerical values not stated.
rows.note: The text reports some success steering completions toward the target year, but efficacy depends on layer, release decade, and target year.
rows.check: Steering efficacy measures causal use of the probe's manifold, not feature dimensionality or superposition. Values are figure-only. The record's V6 label wrongly cites this row.

relationships.condition: Continuous concepts (release year, U.S. geographic coordinates) in Llama 2-7b residual stream, layers 1-32
relationships.reason: Based on the text (Figure 3, Section 4.1; no row captures it): each concept is linearly represented by many features with positive test R2, and space has three strongly predictable ones. So continuous concepts span multiple dimensions, but irreducibility is not tested and the rotated features look like separable directions (R2, R3).
relationships.display_finding: Each concept was linearly represented by many features with positive test R², and space had three strongly predictable ones, so continuous concepts span multiple dimensions. Irreducibility was not tested, and the rotated features look like separable directions.

relation.reason: Superposition supplies the method's statistical framework. The reported demonstrations do not distinguish grouped directional features from irreducibly multidimensional features.

tranche.reason: The probe assumes additive superposition and demonstrates feature recovery, interpretability and steering. Multiple scalar features of a concept do not establish an irreducible multidimensional feature or show V6 needs qualification.

source_check.notes: The paper distinguishes concepts from scalar features of those concepts; multiple features do not settle V6. Steering interventions target the last token of the work's title, using three-dimensional fitted manifolds; numerical efficacy values remain figure-only.

statements.correction: Llama 2-7b, layer 16: Varimax rotation of the top 5 time features and top 32 space features; decade separation and state localization. Section 4.1 reports multiple predictable features. Irreducibility is untested; V6 verdict=none.
statements.problem: The Llama 2 description and unresolved irreducibility are accurate, but the limits_scope classification treats an untested distinction as a demonstrated qualification of V6.
